issues.title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Align NPU IPC reload lifecycle
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Implements **Phase 0 — Restore transaction parity** from RFC #16322.

NPU IPC previously differed from HCCL in two correctness-critical ways: its START/FINISH hooks did not restore checkpoint-facing state or refresh derived state, and its packed receive path decoded weights without calling `model.load_weights`. This PR restores the same START → LOAD → FINISH transaction for both IPC modes and adds unit coverage for the lifecycle and packed loading path.

### State-transition E2E matrix

The E2E oracle is:

1. Start from `--load-format dummy` and successfully infer in `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph mode.
2. Load every parameter of the reduced served model from a complete deterministic fixed-random BF16 payload, then record deterministic text and token logprobs as baseline B.
3. Pause, execute START → LOAD → FINISH with the identical complete payload, resume, and require an exact match with B.
4. Also require the dummy signature to differ from B, preventing a missing first load from passing.

The source enumerates the full served parameter name/shape set from a meta model and generates tensors on demand from a suite seed plus parameter name. It downloads no checkpoint shards or index, stores no persistent second model copy, and permits no allowlist or skipped parameter.

| Transport | Resource lane | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPU IPC | `one_card/rlhf/state_transitions` | unpacked and packed IPC; trainer and worker share one physical NPU through IPC handles |
| HCCL | `two_card/rlhf/state_transitions` | unpacked and packed HCCL broadcast; inference worker on NPU 0 and trainer on NPU 1 |

The HCCL test now parametrizes both modes and passes the same `packed` value to `HCCLWeightTransferUpdateInfo` and `HCCLTrainerSendWeightsArgs`. Its estimated CI duration is adjusted for the doubled matrix.

### Served-model payload alignment

The original fixed-random source used Hugging Face `from_config` names and shapes verbatim. That is insufficient for two models: the served model accepts checkpoint-facing names and layouts, not all HF meta-model names.

- **GLM-5.1:** HF exposes routed experts as fused `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj`; the source expands each tensor into per-expert `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, and `down_proj` names that vLLM's MoE loader accepts. It reduces routed experts to 8 for the single-NPU IPC memory budget.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash BF16:** the source maps HF names to the served compact layout (`wq_a`, `wkv`, `wo_a`, `wo_b`, indexer/compressor names, sinks, and per-expert `w1`/`w3`/`w2`) and corrects expert MLP dimensions to the checkpoint's `moe_intermediate_size=2048`.
- **Qwen3.5-35B-A3B:** uses the text sub-config and applies the `model.language_model.*` prefix exactly once.

The reduced architectures preserve the intended execution paths: Qwen retains three linear-attention and one full-attention layer; DeepSeek retains four layers with `[0, 0, 4, 128]` compression ratios, 8 routed experts, and original top-6 routing; GLM retains four layers, including its dense-to-MoE boundary, with 8 routed experts for the IPC memory budget.

### Validation

- Ruff, Python syntax compilation, and `git diff --check` passed locally.
- The branch is mergeable, DCO passed, and CI pre-commit is running for the latest commit.
- A remote Ascend Qwen HCCL packed run was attempted. It is currently blocked before collection by an incompatible vLLM/vLLM-Ascend checkout: `patch_kv_cache_utils.py` expects `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils._get_packed_kv_cache_groups`, but the installed vLLM exposes only `get_kv_cache_groups`. The remote container also has uncommitted vLLM-Ascend changes, so it must be brought to a matched, clean pair before the hardware result can be attributed to this PR.

Refs #16322. Related dummy-path fix: #16485.

issues.title: [BugFix][Attention][v0.30.0] Fix MXFP8 KV-scale corruption during PD transfers
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

C8 K-scale advanced-index assignment on NPU can materialize a packet-strided cache view and write it back through `IndexPutV2` / `ViewCopy`, overwriting a concurrent KV transfer to an unselected page. Invalid E8M0 scales can then produce NaNs and repeated-exclamation output.

Replace that assignment with a stride-aware Triton byte scatter that writes only the addressed token/head/group elements. Every nonempty call uses Triton; the production CPU fallback is removed. Empty batches return before importing the kernel or accessing cache storage. Keep `num_elements` as a runtime scalar with `do_not_specialize` to reuse compilation across token counts for a fixed layout.

Move the former CPU numerical scatter cases to nightly NPU tests. CPU unit tests verify delegation through a mocked kernel and keep layout/slot-index checks; test-only CPU references remain independent numerical oracles. The dispatch change adds no NPU operation or synchronization and leaves the existing device kernel unchanged.

This release PR also retains the previously validated 397B V-scale restoration: partial asynchronous imports can populate three kernel blocks of a five-block decode manager page while bypassing the ordinary allocation preparation. Restore only static V scales for eligible active C8 consumer requests after Pull receive completion and Mamba copies, before model forward. Scope remains the exact built-in MooncakePullConnector, including its registration aliases, with no synchronous loads. No persistent per-request snapshot state is introduced.

The current follow-up changes only the K-scale dispatch and its tests/documentation. Runner, allocation, transport, V-scale restoration, and the Triton kernel remain unchanged. The V-scale integration/performance discussion is tracked in #19065; main PR #19016 remains on hold. The K-scale-only main PR is #19064.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes intermittent C8 output corruption during concurrent PD transfers. C8, MTP and graph execution remain enabled; there are no API or serving-configuration changes. The C8 cache update path is NPU-only.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Fresh Ascend 950DT run: 58/58 NPU tests passed, zero skips.** Covers full-allocation byte preservation, padded strides, storage offsets, noncontiguous uint8/E8M0 sources, partial tiles, empty batches, ACL graph replay, compilation reuse, and 40 concurrent ACL SDMA interleavings. Tested kernel SHA256: `f4e472e67a11359e60a3782ceb00d669417c5b87aeb3bb03a49243e6af7071f8`.
- Six numerical cases now execute real NPU writes: preservation of unselected dense-view elements; mixed valid/padded slots; all-padding batches; real tokens alongside padding; prefill equivalence to the former read-modify-write reference; and padded-decode equivalence outside the reserved null slot. The obsolete CPU `IndexPut`-operation assertion is replaced by dispatch-contract coverage.
- **50/50 related unit tests passed**, including attention planning, the mocked dispatch contract, quantization wiring, scale layouts and slot-index handling. The operator documentation example also passed.
- Fresh tests use the exact PR kernel and dispatch on an existing 0.30-compatible stack: torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, Triton-Ascend 3.6.0. The three cache-layout helpers match the branch source by AST. Installed serving sources and services were unchanged. Full branch dependency-stack integration remains for PR CI.
- **Prior 35B serving validation of the K-scale fix:** prefill TP2 / decode TP1-DP2, C8 + MTP3 + `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; A/B/A corruption counts **27/512 -> 0/512 -> 3/512**, followed by **2048/2048** churn requests without repeated-exclamation corruption or HTTP failure. The independent unselected-page reproducer changed corruption from **4/40 to 0/40**.
- The historical 35B GPQA run completed **198/198** requests without repeated-exclamation corruption, scored **80.30% (159/198)**, and had **76.80%** weighted MTP acceptance without sustained zero acceptance during active generation. This records recovery from corruption, not task-score equivalence to a reference model.
- **Prior 397B validation of the retained V-scale fix:** controlled four-request A/B/A changed corruption **4/4 -> 0/4 -> 4/4**. The simplified restoration completed GPQA **198/198**, scoring **87.37% (173/198)**, with **76.32%** weighted MTP acceptance and **0/135** active zero-acceptance windows across the original requests, warmup and GPQA interval. A separate kernel-specialization follow-up run also scored **87.37% (173/198)**, with **76.19%** acceptance and **0/90** active zero-acceptance windows. These are historical model runs, not fresh runs of the CPU-fallback removal.
- Prior V-scale cost measurements observed **zero copies across 10,968 steady-decode helper calls** (median host check **4.24 us**). Necessary admission/allocation restoration has nonzero event cost. No end-to-end performance non-regression claim is made.
- Prior isolated compilation measurements for the unchanged device kernel reported **0** extra compilations over six new token counts after layout warmup, versus **6** before the `num_elements` specialization cleanup. Initial layout compilation is still required; this is not a full-model throughput measurement.
- Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, Markdown lint and focused source checks passed. Required `bash format.sh ci` attempts could not complete actionlint bootstrap/shared pre-commit cache setup within the timeout; complete CI remains required. Staged Gitleaks scanning is recorded with this update.

No new model GPQA or end-to-end performance run is claimed for this dispatch-only follow-up. The device kernel is unchanged; numerical, graph and concurrent-transfer behavior were revalidated on NPU.

Reproduction commands in a branch-compatible environment:

```bash
pytest --confcutdir=tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops -q -rs \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_mxfp_k_scale_scatter.py
pytest -q tests/ut/attention/test_attention_c8_mxfp.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_mxfp_k_scale_scatter.py \
  tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mxfp_c8.py
```

issues.title: [Attention][Feature] Implement C8-MXFP (FP8 KV Cache with E8M0 Scales) Support for Ascend A5
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
This pull request implements support for C8-MXFP (FP8 KV cache with E8M0 scales) on Ascend A5 using the QFA (Quant Flash Attention) dual-operator interface. It introduces the `AscendC8MXFPAttentionBackend` and its implementation, handles PA_NZ layout scattering, manages static V scale cache filling, and integrates ModelSlim configuration mapping. It also supports hybrid models by correctly sizing the cache blocks and pages from FP8 bytes.

However, a critical issue was identified in `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` where `k_shape` is constructed incorrectly by omitting the first dimension (`num_blocks`), which will lead to a `ValueError` during unpacking in `_split_hybrid_c8_mxfp_cache_buffer` and an `IndexError` later.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes, it adds support for the `K_DYNAMIC_V_STATIC_MXFP8_PER_CHANNEL` KV cache type for Ascend A5, enabling FP8 KV cache quantization with E8M0 scales.

### How was this patch tested?
The patch includes extensive unit tests covering the QFA query plan, per-step derivations, metadata planning, scale cache shapes, PA_NZ scattering, static V scale cache filling, and hybrid block sizing.
